question: QL on Ozempic pens?
assumption: NY Medicaid / NYRx (program not stated; coverage/QL question defaults to NY Medicaid).
answer: Assuming NY Medicaid/NYRx: **Ozempic® pen is preferred** in the GLP-1 RA–Type 2 Diabetes class. The row/class is marked **CC only**, not **F/Q/D**, so the PDL does **not list a specific Ozempic pen QL**. Criteria shown: confirm FDA-approved/compendia-supported and Medicaid-covered indication; **PA required if used concurrently with a GLP-1 + DPP-IV**. NYRx’s general policy says F/Q/D edits can apply and claim messaging should guide the pharmacy; questions can go to the Clinical Call Center. Most maintenance meds may be dispensed up to **90 days** if otherwise allowed.

ny_medicaid_pharmacy_policy (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09)
NYRx Pharmacy Manual Policy Guidelines (Version 2026-3) > 1.0 General Pharmacy Policy > Frequency, Quantity and Duration (F/Q/D) Limits
[p 14]
Prescription, non-prescription drugs, and medical/surgical supplies may have fixed limits in the amount and/or frequency that can be dispensed. NY Medicaid considers Frequency, Quantity, and Duration (F/Q/D) recommendations made by the Drug Utilization Review (DUR) Board. Some of the drugs/drug classes affected by F/Q/D editing are also included in the Preferred Drug Program (PDP). Therefore, drugs/drug classes that have a preferred status can also be subject to F/Q/D editing.
[p 15]
Policy Guidelines
NYRx
System messaging has been developed to help guide the pharmacists to appropriately submit the claim or to refer to the prescriber.
For certain medical/surgical supplies, if the limit on an item is exceeded, prior approval must be requested with accompanying documentation as to why the limit needs to be exceeded. Quantity and frequency limits are available in the OTC and Supply Fee Schedule section of this manual. Questions on medical/surgical supplies may be referred to the Durable Medical Equipment unit at 800-342-3005. The following links have been provided as helpful resources for information on the PDP, F/Q/D and Step Therapy Programs: https://newyork.fhsc.com/ and http://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/dur/index.htm. Questions on prescription Frequency, Quantity and Duration (F/Q/D) Limits may be referred to the NY Medicaid Clinical Call Center at: (877)309-9493.
cited_evidence.ny_medicaid_pharmacy_policy:p17:
ny_medicaid_pharmacy_policy (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09)
NYRx Pharmacy Manual Policy Guidelines (Version 2026-3) > 1.0 General Pharmacy Policy > Service Limits
[p 17]
90-day Supplies
NYRx allows up to a 90-day supply of most maintenance medications and over the counter drugs. Maintenance medication is a medication taken on a regular basis, often daily, to treat an ongoing or chronic condition or illness such as, but not limited to, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, asthma, depression, mild pain. Prescribers should consider prescribing a 90-day supply once a patient is on a stable dose of maintenance medication. Note: State and federal laws regarding controlled substances and day supply will apply.
Medical/Surgical Supplies
Selected medical/surgical supplies have limits in the amount and frequency that can be dispensed to an eligible Medicaid member. If a member exceeds the limit on an item, prior approval must be requested with accompanying documentation as to why the limits need to be exceeded. For more information, please refer to the Fee Schedule at: https://www.emedny.org/ProviderManuals/DME/index.aspx.
